mismatch.message: C enters the non-Antimagic strength-drain arm, rolls rnd(1), and updates Strength; JavaScript reaches its mcastu.c mcast_weaken_you note_unported gap, so the following spell-selection RNG is consumed instead.

summary: The source-backed strength-drain helper is wired through the spell dispatcher and the production adjacent monster AT_MAGC caller. The final selected v54 replay matches every screen, RNG call, and cursor through all 930 steps, including the prior step-228 divergence.

source.branch: mcast_weaken_you: Antimagic produces shield/resistance feedback; otherwise it announces weakness, derives dmg from m_lev - 6 with a minimum of 1, rounds Half_spell_damage upward, rolls rnd(dmg), calls losestr with the caster-specific death reason and KILLED_BY, clears the killer name, and marks magical resistance unseen.
callers: mcastu.c:mcast_spell MCAST_WEAKEN_YOU calls mcast_weaken_you and clears dmg at lines 840-842; js/mcastu.js now awaits the helper in the corresponding arm.

mcastu.c:castmu calls mcast_spell at line 298; mhitu.c:mattacku AT_MAGC calls castmu at line 930; js/unported_monster_actions.js:attackHeroWithMattacku supplies the production cast adapter and the losestr state-bound losehp/encumberMessage owners.
monmove.c:monmove calls castmu(FALSE,FALSE) only for its undirected spell action; MCAST_WEAKEN_YOU is hostile/directed, so this caller cannot reach the helper.
dependencies: mcastu.c:death_inflicted_by is already implemented in js/mcastu.js and returns the caster-specific cause string.

attrib.c:losestr is already implemented in js/attrib.js; its return is discarded in C, and the production AT_MAGC adapter now binds its losehp and encumberMessage operations to the active state and planner.
mondata.c:monstseesu/monstunseesu, display.c:shieldeff, and rnd.c:rnd are already implemented and used in source order.

evidence: The admitted baseline at challenges/evaluations/baseline-78195d815-v54.json records 228/930 screens, 2894/3548 RNG calls, and 900/930 cursors before the first mismatch; recording SHA e3e51a83f4c3fd646792b1beb9755427da7e9402da660b363855e7018497dd4d and input SHA 45d90454248a4bc3c97d75d60b021c6c51189f320359df542992f70d10d86993.

A targeted scan at commit 9c456e572 reproduces the step-228 C call rnd(1)=1 @ mcast_weaken_you(mcastu.c:481) against a later JavaScript rn2(5)=0 and shows the first screen glyph mismatch at row 0 column 0. The current code names this gap at js/mcastu.js MCAST_WEAKEN_YOU.
Source comparison covered mcastu.c:mcast_weaken_you lines 466-488, its mcast_spell case at 840-842, castmu's mcast_spell call at 298, and mhitu.c:mattacku's AT_MAGC call at 930.

Committed-tree selected scan output .cache/C-v54-rogue-weaken-selected-scan.stdout.json (SHA-256 1e702808834f4755f2b16f1d6b032ff06465c651da01551387a3b58d9578a720) reports divergence=null, no boundary/refusal/error, 930/930 screens and cursors emitted, and recordingMatched=true through step 929; its replay input digest is ac8c8692592aa6bfa307d7feaac05f0cca9aff0635884df470691b358735afd0.

Source-pinned tests cover the Antimagic no-draw arm, the ordinary rnd(m_lev-6) branch with upward Half_spell_damage rounding, attribute loss via losestr, and the MCAST_WEAKEN_YOU dispatcher; production caller reachability is the matching 930-step v54 synthetic replay.
